item.title: Sundance 2026 Movies Sold So Far: ‘Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!’ with Rinko Kikuchi Sells to Sony Pictures Classics
item.description: Josef Kubota Wladyka directed the crowd pleasing film that is the first U.S. Dramatic competition title sold out of Sundance.

item.title: ‘Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story’ Review: Ya Gotta Laugh to Keep from Crying, Right?
item.description: Sundance: If anything, Judd Apatow and Neil Berkeley's documentary about the beloved, wonderfully honest comedian suffers from having too much good material.

item.title: Quentin Tarantino’s New Beverly Cinema Goes Back to Its Porno Roots This February
item.description: The repertory cinema spent most of the 1970s as an adult movie theater called the Eros. February's schedule looks back to that era with hard and softcore entries from Wes Craven, Russ Meyer, Radley Metzger and more.

item.title: ‘The Musical’ Review: A Darkly Comic ‘School of Rock’ for the Era of Stephen Miller
item.description: Will Brill plays a bitter middle school teacher who secretly stages a musical about 9/11 in Giselle Bonilla's very irreverent — but only sometimes funny — debut feature.

item.title: Your First Look at The Beatles Movies Came in a Peculiar Postcard Form
item.description: Students at a performing arts school in Liverpool were given pictures of Harris Dickinson, Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, and Barry Keoghan as John, Paul, George, and Ringo.

item.title: ‘Undertone’ Filmmaker Ian Tuason Learned from All Your Favorite Horror Films to Make His Creepy Hit — but Not in the Ways You Might Expect
item.description: The filmmaker and his stars Nina Kiri and Adam DiMarco stopped by the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox, to unpack the many inspirations for their A24 haunted house thriller.

item.title: The Cast of ‘Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass’ Share Fond Memories of Watching John Slattery Get Kicked in the Groin
item.description: David Wain, Ken Marino, and the film's star-studded ensemble cast visited the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox, to discuss one of the festival's funniest films.

item.title: The Cast and Filmmakers of ‘The Musical’ Will Try Not to Spoil the Dark Comedy’s Big Twist for You
item.description: Director Giselle Bonilla, screenwriter Alex Heller, and stars Rob Lowe, Gillian Jacobs, and Will Brill visited the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox, on the day of their Sundance premiere.

item.title: ‘The Weight’ Review: Ethan Hawke Smuggles Stolen Gold in a ‘Sorcerer’ Homage That Drags Through the Muck
item.description: Sundance: Padraic McKinley's action throwback stars Hawke as a resourceful inmate navigating the Great Depression-era Oregon wilderness — and a plot that can move with a slow, murky trudge.

item.title: ‘If I Go Will They Miss Me’ Review: Walter Thompson-Hernández Delivers an Ambitious Portrait of Black Angelino Life
item.description: In his narrative feature debut, the "Kites" filmmaker uses a tense parental relationship as a way into exploring the Black community of his youth
